evidence: Cic. Arch. 7: sī quī foederātīs cīvitātibus ascrīptī fuissent
terms.comment: Classically of a people bound to Rome by a treaty, foedus (Lewis & Short, s.v. foederō). Used now of the members of a federation; the United States are Cīvitātēs Foederātae (Traupman 180).

terms.gloss: a federal state; a state of the United States
terms.comment: A modern application of the classical word; our sources give no settled term for the federal government as against the states’ (see state, a country).

phrases.latin: data est cīvitās Silvānī lēge et Carbōnis: sī quī foederātīs cīvitātibus ascrīptī fuissent
phrases.english: citizenship was given by the law of Silvanus and Carbo to any who had been enrolled in allied cities

sources: Lewis & Short: foedero · Lewis & Short: foedus · Lewis & Short: civitas
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 180.
Cicero, Pro Archia 7, checked against the Perseus Latin texts (11 November 2026).
